messages:
Lina (product): quick sync  customer A asked for rolling upgrades that preserve egress IPs and an option for customer-managed NAT. they also want a migration path from our current bundle to a slim agent. what are the non-negotiables and where does this land on the roadmap?
Matt (eng): agreed. main technical risks: KV cache invalidation during rolling upgrades, and ensuring model-serving pods can drain without quality/regression. two paths: operator-shim to orchestrate in-cluster upgrades or sidecar-based rolling replace. operator gives more control for canaries and rollbacks.
Sarah (netops): preserving egress IP is the blocker for most enterprise customers. propose supporting: (1) customer-controlled NAT (preferred), (2) static egress via our relay as fallback. also need docs for BGP peering vs static route setups.
Jill (devops): packaging-wise we can ship three installer presets: full (relay+telemetry), slim (minimal agent, expects customer NAT), and airgap (offline tarball). slim requires post-install ip validation and documented hooks for egress pinning.
Lina (product): proposed launch criteria: - rolling upgrade with no >1min p99 latency spike - pinned tenants keep same egress IPs during and after upgrade - slim installer validated by field test on at least 2 customers - rollback steps + canary checklist documented
Matt (eng): action items for testing: build a harness simulating 100 tenants with pinned egress. run rollout: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% and measure KV cache hit-rate, tail latency. add health endpoint `/health/upgrade-ready` to signal graceful-drain status.
Sarah (netops): runbook should include quick BGP example and iptables fallback. e.g., BGP neighbor snippet: `neighbor 10.0.0.1 remote-as 65000` and validation: `curl -sS https://ifconfig.me` (respect privacy notes).
Jill (devops): packaging flags for slim: ```yaml
installer_mode: slim
preserve_egress: true
relay_enabled: false
``` add `--force-ip-check` post-install verification.
Lina (product): prioritization: slot this high in Q2 core infra. enterprise commitments hinge on it. need rough eng estimates for roadmap.
Matt (eng): estimates: operator + canary infra ~4 eng-sprints (2 engineers), packaging + installer presets ~1 sprint (1 engineer), netops docs + tests ~0.5 sprint. field validation with customers adds ~2 weeks across two validation windows. total ~5.5 sprint-equivalents + validation time.
Sarah (netops): plan two validation windows: one for BGP peering, one for customer NAT fallback. expect ~1 week per window. will coordinate with field teams.
Lina (product): owners: @Matt -> PRD stub + canary test plan by Tue. @Jill -> slim installer flags + validation script by Fri. @Sarah -> egress runbook + BGP examples by Thu. @ops-bot -> create tracking ticket in shiproom. speak now if concerns.
Matt (eng): acknowledged, starting PRD stub.
Jill (devops): prototyping `--force-ip-check` tomorrow.
Sarah (netops): pulling sample configs from field.
ops-bot: created ticket RDW-5243: "private-deploy: rolling-upgrade + egress-preservation" assigned to Lina, Matt, Jill, Sarah. :white_check_mark:
Lina (product): thanks all  i'll add estimates to roadmap and ping legal for SLA language. scheduling 30-min walkthrough next Mon.
Matt (eng): +1 for walkthrough.
Jill (devops): added to calendar.
Sarah (netops): will prepare BGP test snippets.
Lina (product): end.
